notes:
Summary: Spectreline builds a VS Code copilot extension (IDEGuard) focused on enterprise customers. Key differentiators: local prefetch agent + hosted model for heavy completions, aggressive inline suggestion latency target, and model pinning per release channel.

What they need / told us on call:
- Streaming-first completions: want token-level streaming to surface inline suggestions as the model generates (target 40-80ms per chunk).
- Low-latency inline suggestions: typical accept threshold <= 120ms for short inline completions, 300ms for larger multi-line completions.
- Model/version pinning: pin "stable" QA-verified model for extension releases, with canary channel using newer model variants. Must be able to rollback quickly.
- Rate limits & auth: per-seat rate limiting + per-workspace burst buckets; integration with SSO for license enforcement.
- Cost sensitivity: extension is PLG with heavy free-tier usage; wants Optimize recommendations to reduce token spend (prefix caching, prompt shortening).
- Offline/fallback mode: small on-device quantized model for basic completions when offline; hosted calls only for full-power completions and code explanation.
- Observability: need per-route latency + token-cost breakdown and trace links to Git commit + file path for debugging.
- Security: SOC2-like controls, audit logs, KMS key support, optional EU residency for enterprise accounts.

Notes from SE session:
- "We need per-file caching to avoid re-sending large license headers repeatedly."
- "If streaming is choppy, devs will disable — latency/packetization matters as much as raw RPS."
- POC asks: 1) integrate Redwood streaming websocket/gRPC in extension; 2) demonstrate model pinning API with canary rollback; 3) show cost delta with/without prefix caching.

Attachments referenced: pricing deck (Drive), security FAQ, initial integration checklist.
